title: Coordinates of the center of mass
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, let $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, and let $i$ be a coordinate. The $i$th coordinate of the center of mass defined by $f$ and $\alpha$ equals the singleton Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $\{i\}$ divided by $\alpha$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
